Fit a time-to-event model that borrows from an external source

cv.bregsurv.Rd

cv.bregsurv() is the main function of the package. It fits a model to your data while borrowing from what an external source made available, by minimizing $$Q_\eta(\theta) = -\ell(\theta) + \eta\, B_G(\theta), \qquad \eta \ge 0,$$ the negative log-likelihood \(\ell\) of your data plus an integration weight \(\eta\) times a Bregman divergence \(B_G\) between your model and the external one. \(\eta = 0\) ignores the external source and larger values borrow more; cv.bregsurv() chooses \(\eta\) (and, under a penalty, the penalty level) by cross-validation on your data.

A call is made of four choices, one per argument:

  1. target: the model you fit to your own data, which fixes \(\ell\);

  2. release: what the external source made available;

  3. divergence: how the release enters the objective, which fixes \(B_G\);

  4. penalty: an optional ridge, lasso or elastic-net penalty on the coefficients.

Usage

cv.bregsurv(
  target,
  release = NULL,
  divergence = NULL,
  penalty = c("none", "ridge", "lasso", "enet"),
  alpha = 0.5,
  etas = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  nlambda = 50,
  lambda.min.ratio = NULL,
  nfolds = 5,
  seed = 20260818L,
  criterion = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

target

The model you fit to your data. Build it with one of three constructors; each takes your data, one row per subject, and checks it:

  • target_cox()(time, event, z, stratum = NULL, ties = "none", score = "linear"): a Cox proportional-hazards model for follow-up recorded as a time and an event indicator.

    • stratum: optional strata, each with its own baseline hazard;

    • ties: how tied event times enter the partial likelihood ("none", "breslow" or "exact").

  • target_ncc()(case, set, z): a nested case-control (matched case-control) design.

    • case: 1 for the case and 0 for the controls;

    • set: the matched set of each row; every set holds exactly one case;

    • the likelihood is the conditional likelihood of which member of each set is the case.

  • target_discrete()(interval, event, z, stratum = NULL, link = "cloglog", score = "linear"): a discrete-time (grouped-time) model for follow-up recorded in intervals \(1, \dots, K\).

    • interval: the last interval each subject was at risk in;

    • event: 1 when the event happened in that interval;

    • link: "cloglog" (grouped proportional hazards) or "logit".

In all three, z holds the covariates (a numeric matrix or data frame, one column per covariate, with names). target_cox() and target_discrete() also take score = nn_score() to replace the linear risk score \(z^\top\beta\) by a neural network (requires the torch package).

release

What the external source made available, or NULL to fit your data alone. Build it with one of four constructors, by what you received:

  • release_records(): individual records, another cohort's data subject by subject, in the target's design and with your covariate names.

    • z: the external covariates;

    • time, event (and optionally stratum) for a Cox target;

    • case, set for a nested case-control target;

    • interval, event for a discrete-time target.

  • release_coef()(beta, Q = NULL): a fitted model, with or without its uncertainty.

    • beta: its coefficients, named by covariate, every name one of your covariates; covariates the model does not include are set to 0;

    • Q: its uncertainty, the precision matrix of the coefficients (the inverse of their covariance matrix), when it was published.

  • release_score()(score): a risk score without survival probabilities, when the external model is available only through its score for each of your subjects.

    • score: one value per row of your data, in the same order, on the scale of a linear predictor.

  • release_model(): survival probabilities, an external model's absolute risks. A discrete-time target needs this form for the Kullback-Leibler divergence.

    • beta with baseline: the external Cox coefficients and the increments of its baseline cumulative hazard over your intervals \(1, \dots, K\);

    • or hazard: the external interval hazards of your subjects, an \(n \times K\) matrix.

divergence

How the release enters the objective, i.e. which Bregman divergence \(B_G\) is used. NULL (the default) takes the first one the release supports, in the order listed in Details.

  • "composite": the external records' own log-likelihood is added with weight \(\eta\), giving a composite likelihood in which the two cohorts share the coefficients and keep their own baselines. Needs release_records().

  • "mahalanobis": the Mahalanobis distance \(\frac{1}{2}(\beta - \tilde\beta)^\top Q (\beta - \tilde\beta)\) to the external coefficients \(\tilde\beta\); the Euclidean distance on the covered covariates when the release has no Q. Needs coefficients: release_coef() or release_model(), or on a Cox target release_records(), from which a Cox model is fitted.

  • "kl": the Kullback-Leibler divergence between the distributions the two models predict for your subjects (who fails at each event time for a Cox target, which member of a set is the case for a matched design, the hazard of each interval for a discrete-time target). It needs only the external model's predictions, so it works with release_coef(), release_score() and release_model(); on a discrete-time target only with release_model(). It is the only divergence defined for a neural target.

  • "none": no borrowing, your data alone (\(\eta = 0\)); the only choice when release = NULL.

penalty

Penalty on the coefficients of a linear target:

  • "none" (the default);

  • "ridge": \(\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\);

  • "lasso": \(\lambda\|\beta\|_1\), which sets some coefficients to zero;

  • "enet": the elastic net \(\lambda\{\alpha\|\beta\|_1 + \frac{1-\alpha}{2}\|\beta\|_2^2\}\).

A neural target is regularized by early stopping and dropout instead and takes "none".

alpha

Elastic-net mixing parameter for penalty = "enet", in \((0, 1]\).

etas

Candidate integration weights. NULL uses a grid that starts at 0 (your data alone) and is log spaced from 0.01 to an upper end suited to the divergence.

lambda, nlambda, lambda.min.ratio

The penalty path: given values in lambda, or nlambda log-spaced values from the smallest penalty that sets every coefficient to zero down to lambda.min.ratio times it, built for each eta.

nfolds

Number of cross-validation folds.

seed

Seed of the fold assignment. The default is fixed, so repeated calls, and calls with different releases or divergences on the same target, share one partition and their values can be compared directly.

criterion

Cross-validation criterion. A Cox target uses "V&VH" (the partial-likelihood loss of Verweij and Van Houwelingen) by default and also accepts "LinPred", "CIndex_pooled" and "CIndex_foldaverage"; a nested case-control target uses "loss" (the conditional log-likelihood) and also accepts "AUC", "CIndex" and "Brier"; a discrete-time target uses the held-out negative log-likelihood per subject. Fits are comparable only under the same criterion.

standardize

Standardize the covariates before penalizing; coefficients are always returned on the original scale.

...

Further arguments passed to the estimator that fits the model (named in the result's engine).

Value

An object of class "cv.bregsurv", a list with

eta, lambda

The selected integration weight and penalty level.

value, criterion

The cross-validated value of the selected fit and its criterion.

coefficients

The coefficients of the selected fit (linear targets).

coefficients_target_only

The coefficients at \(\eta = 0\), when 0 is in etas.

coefficients_external

The external coefficients aligned to your covariates, when the release has coefficients.

gamma

For a discrete-time target, the baseline parameters of the selected fit (one row per stratum, one column per interval, on the link scale).

path

The cross-validated value at each eta (at its best lambda under a penalty).

folds, seed

The cross-validation partition.

engine, fit

The estimator that was called and its complete result.

divergence, penalty, target, release

The choices that were made.

Use plot() for the cross-validation curve and the coefficients, coef() and predict() for the fitted model.

Details

Which divergences a release supports. The first divergence in each cell is the default.

releaseCoxnested case-controldiscrete timeneural target
NULLnonenonenonenone
release_records(): individual recordscomposite, mahalanobis, klcompositecomposite–
release_coef(): a fitted model without its uncertaintykl, mahalanobiskl, mahalanobismahalanobiskl (Cox only)
release_coef(): a fitted model with its uncertaintymahalanobis, klmahalanobis, klmahalanobiskl (Cox only)
release_score(): a risk score without survival probabilitiesklkl–kl (Cox only)
release_model(): survival probabilitiesas release_coef()as release_coef()kl, mahalanobiskl

Which estimator fits the model. A linear target is fitted by one of the package's estimators, named in the result's engine; the result is identical to calling that estimator directly.

divergenceCoxnested case-controldiscrete time
"kl", "none"cv.coxkl()cv.ncckl()cv.discretekl()
"mahalanobis"cv.cox_MDTL()cv.ncc_MDTL()cv.discrete_MDTL()
"composite"cv.cox_indi()cv.ncc_indi()cv.discrete_indi()

with the suffix _ridge for penalty = "ridge" and _enet for "lasso" and "enet" (for example cv.coxkl_enet()), and cv.coxkl_ties() for ties = "exact". "none" is the Kullback-Leibler estimator at \(\eta = 0\). A neural target is trained with torch.

See also

bregsurv() to fit at a given eta; the targets target_cox(), target_ncc(), target_discrete(); the releases release_records(), release_coef(), release_score(), release_model(); plot.cv.bregsurv(), predict.cv.bregsurv().

Examples

data(ExampleData_lowdim)
tr <- ExampleData_lowdim$train
target <- target_cox(time = tr$time, event = tr$status, z = tr$z)

# an external risk score without survival probabilities, for each of your subjects
kl <- cv.bregsurv(target, release_score(ExampleData_lowdim$score_external$train), divergence = "kl")
kl
#> Target:     Cox model
#> Divergence: Kullback-Leibler
#> Selected:   eta = 1.104
#> CV V&VH: 2.51343  (5 folds, seed 20260818)
#> Engine:     cv.coxkl
#> 
#> Coefficients:
#>      Z1      Z2      Z3      Z4      Z5      Z6 
#>  0.1950 -0.1987  0.0077 -0.3929  0.2768 -0.3619 

# a fitted model without its uncertainty, through the Euclidean distance
euc <- cv.bregsurv(target, release_coef(ExampleData_lowdim$beta_external_fair),
                   divergence = "mahalanobis")

# your data alone; all three share one partition, so the values compare directly
own <- cv.bregsurv(target)
c(target_only = own$value, kl = kl$value, euclidean = euc$value)
#> target_only          kl   euclidean 
#>    2.624735    2.513432    2.511217
